source: Hand-written by the Interim team (2026-10-10) from the SNOMED CT concepts present in the committed Synthea run; semantic tags are the parenthesised suffix SNOMED prints on every fully specified name.
rationale: A participant's comorbidity list (participants.json) and the conditions diagnosed at a note's encounter (notes.json ground truth) should be clinical problems a research nurse would record as medical history. Synthea also emits social-determinant and administrative 'conditions' (employment, education, criminal record, intimate partner abuse, refugee status, 'medication review due'), which are not medical history, are sensitive even when synthetic, and would be noise in a chart-scan answer key. Rule: keep a condition when its semantic tag is not in exclude_semantic_tags, or when its code is in allow_snomed (clinically relevant findings/situations); always drop codes in exclude_snomed. A condition with no semantic tag (Synthea prints 'Opioid abuse' bare) is kept. NSCLC itself is reported separately (participants[].nsclc) and never listed as a comorbidity; its codes are in import_tables.json.
